text:
Debauchery and Death are two good girls,

Lavish with their kisses and rich in health,

Whose virginal flank, covered by rags,

Under eternal sowing never bore fruit.


To the sinister poet, blemish of families,

Favorite of hell, unpaid courtier,

Within their recesses, tomb and brothel show

A bed that anxiety never frequented,


And coffin and alcove, in fertile blasphemies,

By turns offer us, like good sisters,

Frightful pleasures and horrendous sweetnesses.


Filthy License, when at last will you bury me?

When will you come, Death, her fascinating rival,

To graft your cypresses onto her infected myrtles?

translation.title: The Two Good Sisters
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the blasphemous pairing of debauchery and death as sisterly consolations.
